5. SEPARATE REQUIREMENTS AND USE

c.textvalue: Front cap face to back of front facing

report.paragraph: Front strap clearance and cap-to-facing clearance are separate measurements. Keep the front face of the cap at least 24 inches from the back of facing. The cap is shown in plan for coordination; no elevation strap/cap clearance is solved here.

The side-wall 24-inch pile-face offset is the specified layout criterion for this task. SDG 3.13.2.N.2.i applies 24 inches to cap/front-facing clearance; N.2.ii applies it to battered pile/leveling-pad clearance. Those provisions are not a side-wall strap-clearance calculation.

Pile placement tolerance is excluded as requested. Skew may be reversed around the nominal pile, but this does not demonstrate clearance for all possible as-built positions or the full reinforcement route. Coordinate actual pile positions and adjacent obstructions separately.

Only the front wall is checked for nominal centered-strap geometry. Side reinforcement, rear walls, elevation routing, reinforcement length, connection/development and wall stability are outside this module. No side or overall wall-design pass is implied.

The plan assumes wall faces parallel to these axes. Nominal pile width defines the clearance; the tiny saved frame rotation is retained for pile centers and the cap outline. The open boundary has no rear edge or rear-wall requirement.
